Caspersen Beach Park.alt: The sun setting low over the Gulf, with waves breaking white around dark limestone rocks in the shallows of Caspersen Beach
Caspersen Beach Park.caption: Sunset over the rocky shallows of Caspersen Beach in Venice, photographed in December 2014.
Caspersen Beach Park.author: Grendelkhan
Caspersen Beach Park.modificationNotice: Resized, cropped for display and converted to WebP. The adaptation is released under the same licence.
Caspersen Beach Park.verification: Commons file 'Sunset at Caspersen Beach' by Grendelkhan, CC BY-SA 4.0, 23 Dec 2014; description 'The sun setting over the ocean as seen from Caspersen Beach in Venice, Florida', geotag 27.056376,-82.443202 on Caspersen Beach. Visually: the dark rock outcrops and boulders in the surf that distinguish Caspersen from Venice's other sand beaches (same rocks seen in the author's aerial view of the beach). No people. Pre-dates the 2024 hurricane damage. Live Commons licence checked: CC BY-SA 4.0.

Venice Museum.alt: The cream stucco Triangle Inn, a two-story Mediterranean Revival building with a round tower, green tile roof and arched windows, with a banner reading Venice Archives at the Historic Triangle Inn by the entrance
Venice Museum.caption: The historic Triangle Inn on Nassau Street, home of the Venice Museum and Archives, photographed in 2010 when its banner read Venice Archives.
Venice Museum.author: Ebyabe

Venice Museum.verification: Commons file 'Venice FL Triangle Inn03' by Ebyabe, CC BY-SA 3.0, taken 2010-10-21; description links the Triangle Inn in Venice, Florida (companion file Inn01 geotagged 27.095,-82.447778). Visually: the Mediterranean Revival Triangle Inn with its round tower, and a banner at the entrance reading 'Venice Archives At The Historic Triangle Inn, 351 Nassau St.' - the building that houses the Venice Museum & Archives (the institution has since used the Venice Museum name; caption notes the 2010 banner). No people. Live Commons licence checked: CC BY-SA 3.0.
